title: Targeting hexose phosphate transport regulatory protein A with the herbal-small molecule honokiol induces carbon starvation under nutrient stress to combat methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection.
authors: Wei, Chi; Guo, Yujia; Zhan, Jiaying; Zheng, Jinjin; Yu, Bin; Xu, Haodong; Yang, Yu; Bai, Jingwen
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子厚朴酚靶向细菌HptA蛋白以抗MRSA感染，虽含分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) compromises chronic wound healing, and growing antibiotic resistance necessitates novel agents that target unconventional bacterial vulnerabilities. PURPOSE: To investigate the anti-MRSA efficacy of honokiol and to characterize hexose phosphate transport regulatory protein A (HptA), a regulator of alternative carbon source uptake under nutritional stress, as a therapeutic target. METHODS: Anti-MRSA activity was evaluated in vitro, with MIC determination. HptA protein was purified, and HptA-honokiol interactions were characterized using molecular docking, bio-layer interferometry, and related techniques. Multi-omics analysis were performed to elucidate metabolic responses. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in mouse model of MRSA-induced wound infection. RESULTS: Honokiol exhibited moderate anti-MRSA activity with an MIC of 36 microg/ml. Mechanistically, honokiol allosterically locks HptA into a nonfunctional conformation, blocking glucose-6-phosphate uptake under nutrient-limited wound conditions. This induces carbon starvation, redox imbalance, and a ROS burst, leading to membrane damage, DNA fragmentation, and biofilm eradication. Local bacterial clearance subsequently reduced peptidoglycan-driven TLR2/NF-kappaB activation, attenuated inflammation, and significantly accelerated wound healing in vivo. CONCLUSION: HptA is identified as a potential antibacterial target against MRSA. By blocking alternative carbon uptake, honokiol induces carbon starvation‑driven lethal stress; lowered bacterial burden then inhibits TLR2/NF‑kappaB signaling, accelerating wound healing through a localized antibacterial action.
abstract_zh: 背景：耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌（Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, MRSA）损害慢性伤口愈合，且日益增长的抗生素耐药性要求开发针对非常规细菌弱点的新型药物。目的：研究厚朴酚（honokiol）的抗MRSA效力，并将己糖磷酸转运调节蛋白A（HptA）——一种在营养胁迫下调节替代碳源摄取的调控因子——表征为治疗靶点。方法：通过体外实验评估抗MRSA活性，并测定最低抑菌浓度（MIC）。纯化HptA蛋白，利用分子对接、生物层干涉法及相关技术表征HptA-厚朴酚相互作用。进行多组学分析以阐明代谢响应。在MRSA诱导的伤口感染小鼠模型中评估治疗效果。结果：厚朴酚表现出中等抗MRSA活性，MIC为36微克/毫升。机制上，厚朴酚将HptA变构锁定为非功能构象，在营养受限的伤口条件下阻断葡萄糖-6-磷酸摄取。这诱导碳饥饿、氧化还原失衡和活性氧爆发，导致膜损伤、DNA断裂和生物膜清除。局部细菌清除随后减少肽聚糖驱动的TLR2/NF-kappaB激活，减轻炎症，并在体内显著加速伤口愈合。结论：HptA被确定为针对MRSA的潜在抗菌靶点。通过阻断替代碳摄取，厚朴酚诱导碳饥饿驱动的致死性胁迫；降低的细菌负荷随后抑制TLR2/NF-kappaB信号传导，通过局部抗菌作用加速伤口愈合。
